arxiv-2605-08810: Short-video apps choose each next clip from millions of candidates, and reading raw video for every option is prohibitively expensive. arxiv-2605-09710: Quantum nonlocality usually needs entanglement — but remarkably, not always. arxiv-2605-10010: Generalized linear equations over a finite group resist approximation — optimally so. Amey Bhangale and Yezhou Zhang prove the optimal inapproximability. plos-pone-0003410: Doctors tested a practical question about bird-flu treatment in this 2008 clinical paper. plos-pone-0003510: Microbiologists catalogued the ulcer bug's secreted weapons in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003610: Nanotechnologists Ghatkesar, Lang, and Gerber weighed molecules by bending beams in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003710: In 2008, Nygren and Bryder built a way to trace blood stem cells' family history. Their new assay reads how many times hematopoietic stem cells have divided inside a living animal. plos-pone-0003810: Thibonnier, Thiberge, and De Reuse found the ulcer bug can't live without its rescue squad in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003910: In 2008, a team found mouse muscles aging fast without one control protein. Muscles missing serum response factor, or SRF, showed early aging: wasting, fat buildup, and scarring. plos-pone-0004010: In 2008, Leimu and Fischer asked if plants really are hometown specialists. Their meta-analysis pooled dozens of studies of local adaptation across plant species. plos-pone-0004110: In 2009, Haag, Pontes, and Pikaard probed plant-only gene silencers. The metal A and metal B sites of Pol IV and Pol V proved essential for siRNA-driven DNA methylation. The plant-specific polymerases anchor a unique silencing system. The work maps their catalytic heart.
plos-pone-0004210: In 2009, Jin, Tyler-Smith, and Kim traced Korea's deep roots. Mitochondrial DNA and Y-chromosome markers revealed the peopling of ancient Korea. plos-pone-0004310: In 2009, Louie, Yang, and Conrad found a new dial on a key pathway. The Dishevelled-associated protein Hipk1 tuned beta-catenin signaling. plos-pone-0357010: Deep dry needling — inserting thin needles into muscle trigger points — is popular for leg pain, but its effects on how the foot bears weight were unclear. plos-pone-0348110: Northeast China’s black soils are among the world’s most fertile — and their history is written in sediment. plos-pone-0357310: Geography textbooks teach more than maps — they teach what science itself is. The critique pushes for textbooks that show science as inquiry and argument, not just a list of facts.
plos-pone-0355210: Benzodiazepine-related deaths are rising — and the patterns behind them matter for prevention. The data give coroners and policymakers a clear, unsparing picture of who is dying and how.
plos-pone-0357910: Heart disease patients live with gnawing uncertainty — and it quietly erodes their quality of life. The pathways reveal exactly where interventions could break the destructive chain.
plos-pone-0357410: Community children’s cafeterias feed kids — and could teach them health too. The program reaches children exactly where they eat, turning mealtime into learning time.
plos-pone-0357110: A little-known mouth bacterium may be driving gum disease. The synthesized findings link the microbe to diseased gums — a potential new target for prevention and treatment.
plos-pone-0356910: Cities can’t reduce waste without cooperation across the whole network. The game-theoretic analysis guides policies that make collaboration — not free-riding — the rational choice.
plos-pone-0350910: Food safety in a rural Thai community improved when the community itself took charge. plos-pone-0354510: Virtual reality that reads your brainwaves could adapt itself to your pain. This paper built a personalized adaptive VR experience driven by EEG-based pain recognition. plos-pone-0355710: Good teaching can be observed — but only with a valid instrument. This paper developed and validated the OPTIS observation protocol for teaching principles in schools. plos-pone-0345910: How saturated a cell’s fats are ripples through its entire stress-response network. plos-pone-0355410: Fresh fruit surfaces can harbor drug-resistant, biofilm-forming Enterococcus faecalis — a public health concern. This paper documented the risk. The findings remind consumers and regulators that ‘fresh’ doesn’t mean sterile — and that produce safety needs microbial vigilance.
europmc-pmc2816710: The gut microbes of people with type 2 diabetes look different from those of healthy people. europmc-pmc2821410: The protein SIRT1, famous from aging research, also puts the brakes on a major growth pathway. europmc-pmc2873910: Epilepsy runs in families but its genes hide. This 2010 paper scans for genome-wide copy number variation in epilepsy, finding novel susceptibility spots in generalized and focal forms. The authors' scan revealed new leads. Their work advanced the genetic map of seizures.
europmc-pmc2890410: Money, schooling, and power shape whether mothers get care. europmc-pmc2903510: Aches and pains bring millions to family doctors. This 2010 study measures how often regional muscle and joint problems bring patients in each year. The authors' observational data shows the true load on clinics. Their numbers help plan muscle-and-joint care.
europmc-pmc2942810: Grown-up ADHD needed one shared playbook, and this 2010 paper writes it. The authors forge a Europe-wide pact on spotting and treating adult ADHD. Their pact steadied care across borders. The statement still guides clinics today. It settled long fights over diagnosis rules.
europmc-pmc2946910: Gene networks can be read from expression data with the right math. This 2010 paper infers control networks from gene activity data using tree-based methods. europmc-pmc3012610: Zebrafish carry a full detox gene set. This 2010 paper lists all the fish's P450 detox genes and when each switches on. The authors' catalog aids poison testing. Their work backs the fish model. Drug safety screens run faster in fish tanks.
europmc-pmc3048210: A BRAF typo darkens colon cancer outlook. This 2011 paper shows the BRAF mutation forecasts worse outcomes in advanced bowel cancer. The authors' data guides cancer doctors. Their work shaped treatment. BRAF blockers later offered new hope. Testing for the typo is now routine.
europmc-pmc3055910: Protein sizes got measurable three ways. This 2009 paper shows how spinning, sieving, and imaging reveal a protein's size and shape. The author's methods became textbook material. europmc-pmc6591610: Twenty years, 45 countries, 200+ hospitals: the SENTRY program tracked which germs cause bloodstream infections and how drug resistance shifted from 1997 to 2016. europmc-pmc6611910: The mTOR pathway is the cell's growth thermostat - sensing nutrients and deciding whether to build or recycle. europmc-pmc6688310: Health research has long sidelined Indigenous peoples - studying them without them. europmc-pmc6738410: Telomeres - the protective caps on chromosomes - shrink with age and disease. europmc-pmc6751310: Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS - different diseases, one shared fire: brain inflammation.
